title: Your Campaign Title
summary: A one or two sentence hook shown in the marketplace. Make it compelling — this is the pitch.
world: Describe your setting here. Include geography, history, tone, major threats, and any factions the player might encounter. This text is injected into the DM system prompt every single turn, so write it like DM prep notes: specific, useful, and not too long. Aim for 2–4 paragraphs. Example: 'The city of Vareth sprawls across three volcanic islands connected by ancient stone bridges. It is ruled by the Merchant Syndicate, a council of seven trading houses whose public smiles hide a brutal private war for dominance. The streets are safe by day and genuinely dangerous by night — not from monsters, but from Syndicate enforcers and the desperate people they've squeezed dry. Magic is legal but heavily taxed; street witches operate out of back alleys for those who can't afford the licensed practitioners.'
openingScene: Describe the situation at the moment play begins. This primes the AI DM with your intended starting scene before the player types their first action. Write in second-person present tense. 1–2 paragraphs. Example: 'You are standing outside the locked door of the Harbormaster's office with a body at your feet and the sound of boots on cobblestones getting closer. The body belongs to a man you've never seen before, but the knife in his chest is yours — stolen from your room at the inn three hours ago. You have about thirty seconds before whoever is running those boots rounds the corner.'
rulesNotes: Write DM guidance here. This is also injected every turn. Include: recommended character level, any special mechanics (resource tracking, environmental hazards), encounter balance notes, key NPC names and personalities, the win condition, and tone. Example: 'Recommended level: 4–6. Tone: political thriller, morally grey, no clear heroes or villains. Key NPCs: Syndic Orvala (House Corren, 50s, ruthless pragmatist, secretly terrified of losing power); Mira (street witch, 30s, sardonic, owes the player a favor — or will, if they help her first); the Harbormaster (already dead — his death is the inciting incident, and the cause is the central mystery). The campaign ends when the player either exposes the conspiracy publicly, destroys one of the seven houses, or is bought off and leaves Vareth. Standard D&D 5e. Investigation (INT) and Persuasion/Deception (CHA) checks are the primary tools.'
